x.around: Call taxis (aka hotel taxis) are all-white with company decals on the doors, and they can be found lurking around major hotels. Usually ordered by phone, these are usually fairly nice and will take you where you want to go with a minimum of fuss, but charge steeper prices: KD 3 is the standard fare for most trips around town, while going to/from the airport is KD 5.

hidden.d: Stripped of many artifacts during the war – part of it has been renovated and is now open to the public for display.
Kuwait's largest urban park and is a cultural platform with cutting-edge architecture and works of art. It has a museum, botanical garden, monuments, fountains, jogging paths and much more.

x.intro: Kuwait City (Arabic: مدينة الكويت Madīnat al-Kuwayt) is the capital of Kuwait.

must.d: Kuwait's unofficial symbol, found on everything except the flag, are Kuwait's top attraction. Designed by Swedes, built by Yugoslavs, and opened in 1979, they're actually rather interesting up close, as the spheres are covered…
Across from the Seif Palace and about 400 east of the National Museum. Guided tours by friendly Kuwaitis are available for tourists. Women can borrow a proper dress from the mosque in order to enter.
The National Assembly is the seat of the Kuwaiti parliament and is one of the few pieces of fine architecture in the country.
Built in 1896, the interior features original Islamic mosaic tile work, though these suffered badly during the Iraqi occupation.
Artificial island and marine park opened in 1988. Its coastline offers great bird's-eye views of the Kuwait City skyline.

x.safe: Kuwait City is relatively safe. Crime rates are low and the neighboring civil conflict in Iraq has not spilled over into Kuwait. The same is not true of some of the suburbs where it can be unsafe for single females to walk alone. Cars will pull up demanding that western women get in and they can be very threatening.

cities.d: (Al Jahra) – home to the historic Kuwaiti Red Fort

x.intro: Jahra, also referred to as Al Jahra, is the capital of Al Jahra Governorate, Kuwait. It is home to the historic Kuwaiti Red Fort, the site of the 1920 Battle of Jahra.

must.d: Also known as the Red Palace, this historic fort and museum was the site of the 1920 Battle of Jahra, which took place during the Kuwait-Najd War.

cities.d: the closest southern suburb, about 10 min from Kuwait City by car

x.intro: Hawally is the capital of the Hawalli Governorate, a district in the State of Kuwait, about 6 km south of Kuwait City. Hawally is a large suburb and the commercial center for most computer-related goods in Kuwait. Prior to the first Gulf War, it housed a large number of Palestinians, but many were expelled after the war. Hawally is home to many of the Arab and other expat populations in Kuwait. Hawalli governorate's population as of June 30, 2012 was 820,802 residents.

intro: Kuwait (Arabic: الكويت) is a monarchy situated at the Persian Gulf, nestled between Iraq and Saudi Arabia. Historically, Kuwait was a strategic trade port between Mesopotamia, India, and Persia. Like many of its neighbours, Kuwait is endowed with oil and gas wealth.
